2014 / Global / Language Digitization Initiative

Language digitalization (Translation Commons)

Translation Commons supports Indigenous and marginalized language communities by creating open tools, guidelines, and resources that help bring more languages into digital spaces.

Visit project website

**Translation Commons** is a nonprofit language-technology initiative working to make sure that more communities can use their languages fully in digital spaces. Through projects such as the Language Digitization Initiative, Translation Commons provides open resources, guidelines, training, and tools that support Indigenous and marginalized language communities in bringing their languages online. The project is a strong example of design and technology serving cultural sustainability: it helps preserve endangered languages, expands access to information, supports linguistic diversity, and creates shared knowledge resources that communities can adapt for their own needs.

From an SD Standard perspective, Translation Commons connects especially well with criteria related to **Endangered Languages, Cultural Diversity, Accessibility, Open Intellectual Property, Education**, and **Social Gaps**, showing how communication systems can help protect cultural identity while increasing participation in digital life.

Criteria

  • C3 / CultureLocal Culture

    The project adapts to local and regional cultures.

  • C2 / CultureIndigenous Culture

    The project preserves or nurtures Indigenous culture other than language.

  • C1 / CultureEndangered Languages

    The project helps to preserve endangered languages, particularly Indigenous languages.

  • S17 / SocietyEducational Component

    The product includes an educational component that promotes sustainability to the consumer.

  • C7 / CultureCommunity Participation

    The design entity actively supports and participates in the sustainable development of their community.

  • C6 / CultureAudience Engagement

    The project engages end users throughout the design process or audiences that will be directly impacted by the project.

  • CM5 / CultureCultural Policy

    The design entity and the majority of suppliers have a publicly-accessible policy to actively protect and support communities.

  • C4 / CultureCultural Diversity

    The project promotes or enhances cultural diversity.

Data visualizations - Global warming

One of the most iconic data visualizations of the last decade is the Show Your Stripes graphic, representing global warming on a planetary level, between 1850 and 2025, an increase of 1.4°.

Front-of-Package Food Warning Labels

Across Latin America, food warning labels have become one of the clearest examples of communication design used as part of public health policies. In addition to the use of small nutrition tables, or technical nutrition data, these “Excess Sugar,” “Excess Sodium,” “Excess Calories,” or “Excess Saturated Fats” labels are prominently placed on the front of food and beverage packaging.
